label: copy-phase j input late in the sequence, about to output 0 (or j)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase. 97% of activation mass falls on steps where the fed-back input is j; the remaining ~3% is on input 0 when 0 is also the output. It is silent in the original and delimiter phases and on every other input token. Within copy-phase j inputs it is sparse (about 4% of them fire). It is gated by position: nothing before recall_idx 3, and the rate rises toward the end of long (L=8-9) sequences. Magnitude is largest when the token being output is 0, i.e. the original contained the bigram j 0; all top examples are j->0 at recall_idx 5-6. j->j is the next most common case, and other outputs (e, f, z) give weaker activations. Predicate j->{0,j} at recall_idx>=3 reaches dev F1 0.56 and mass recall 0.75; j->0 alone has about 0.92 precision at recall_idx>=4 but misses weaker activations.
